messages:
simon: quick follow-up from the kernel/attention RFC — we need a small ops playbook for runtime rollout controls (per-model flags + fallback kernels) so oncall can react without digging into code :wave:
ava: agreed. root problem is we have 3 overlapping knobs: global feature flag, per-model opt-in, and runtime fallback mapping. folks are confused which to touch in incidents :confused:
priya: can we standardize naming first? suggestion: `kernel_flag.<model_id>.<kernel_variant>` for per-model enabling, and `kernel_fallback_policy` for routing fallback order. that makes tracing in logs easier. :thumbsup:
lin: +1 on naming. also we should record telemetry events for flag flips: `flag.changed`, `flag.applied_to_request`, `fallback.invoked` with reason codes. ops-bot: noted — I'll add those events to the schema ticket. :robot_face:
simon: perfect. also need explicit rollout rules: how we do canary (pct of requests), time window, automatic revert if latency/error spike. minimal SLO guardrails.
ava: proposed initial rollout steps:
- 1) create per-model flag OFF by default
- 2) enable on small canary lane (1%) for 10m
- 3) monitor latency/success/eval-score delta for prompt set
- 4) increase to 10% if metrics stable for 1h
- 5) full enable + remove canary after 24h stable
priya: add fallback mapping at each step: if kernel_fallback_policy contains `soft-fallback` then runtime will try kernel B then A; if `hard-fallback` then immediate (no retry) fall back to compatible model variant.
lin: we need clear ops commands. proposal:
```
# enable per-model kernel
redwoodctl flag set kernel_flag.model-abc.qkv-quant --enabled true --canary 1
# rollback
redwoodctl flag set kernel_flag.model-abc.qkv-quant --enabled false
# observe fallback rate
redwoodctl metrics query "fallback.invoked{model='model-abc'}"
```
simon: love it. let's also include threshold-based auto-revert in the runtime: if p95 latency increases > 30% or error rate > 0.5% over baseline in 5m then auto-disable flag + create incident note.
ava: telemetry fields to capture per request: model_id, kernel_variant, flag_source (per-model/global/default), fallback_reason (kv_cache_miss, kernel_crash, out_of_memory), latency_ms, tokens_generated. that should make triage fast.
priya: agree — we'll need a dashboard tile for `fallback.invoked` per model and `flag.apply_rate` over time. add an eval-run metric: `quality.regression.delta` comparing canary outputs to baseline on our invariant prompt set.
lin: one tricky tradeoff: some kernels are faster but degrade quality slightly. we should expose a strategy: `safety-first`, `latency-first`, `cost-balanced`. rollout policy picks which fallback to choose based on strategy.
simon: good call. keep default `cost-balanced` for experiments, `safety-first` for prod-critical customers.
ava: ops playbook snippets for oncall:
- Step 0: identify spike -> query `fallback.invoked` and `kernel.errors` in last 10m
- Step 1: if fallback rate > 1% and errors rising, set per-model flag to previous kernel: `redwoodctl flag set kernel_flag.<model>.<prev> --enabled true`
- Step 2: if latency spike, flip `kernel_flag.<model>.<kernel_variant>` -> false and enable `kernel_fallback_policy=hard-fallback` for that model
- Step 3: notify engineering + run targeted evals (use `devex-run-eval model-abc canary-set`)
- Step 4: if auto-revert triggered, follow incident runbook to postmortem
priya: who owns adding dashboard and the redwoodctl subcommands? assignable?
simon: ops-bot, can you create tickets: one for telemetry events, one for redwoodctl flags, one for dashboard tiles, one for auto-revert logic? tag owners: priya (runtime), lin (observability), ava (runbooks)
ops-bot: created tickets: #INF-5452 (telemetry schema), #INF-5453 (redwoodctl flags), #INF-5454 (dashboard tiles), #INF-5455 (auto-revert). Assignees: priya, lin, ava respectively. ETA: priya - 2w, lin - 1w, ava - 3d. :white_check_mark:
lin: I'll start dashboard PR Monday and add fallback.invoked panel + quality delta.
priya: I'll draft the flag API and mock `redwoodctl` UX, post RFC in eng-runtime. will include code snippet for default config:
```
kernel_flag:
  model-abc:
    enabled: false
    canary_pct: 0
    strategy: cost-balanced
kernel_fallback_policy:
  model-abc:
    order: [qkv-quant, q8n, cpu-ref]
    mode: soft-fallback
```
simon: small ask: include an audit log entry for any manual flag toggle with who/when/reason. compliance wants traceability.
ava: noted. we'll store flag-change events as `flag.change` with user and reason metadata.
priya: ok I'll include audit in the flag API design.
lin: any objections to landing a minimal playbook + telemetry this sprint and iterating? :eyes:
simon: no objections. ACTION: priya to post the follow-up RFC with flag API by EOD Wednesday. lin to create dashboard PR by Monday. ava to add ops playbook to runbooks. ops-bot to keep tickets updated.
ava: thanks everyone. will sync in tomorrow eng-runtime standup. :party_popper: "
